title: Decoupled prompt-bundle ACLs, signing, and deterministic fingerprints
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Purpose: create a maintainable, auditable structure for curated prompt bundles used as eval golden datasets that separates access control (ACLs), cryptographic signing, and content-addressed versioning (deterministic fingerprints). This ticket scopes the PM requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout strategy, and high-level UX for bundle authors and consumers.

Goals:
- Ensure every golden prompt bundle has a deterministic fingerprint (content-addressed hash) that is stable across metadata-only edits.
- Allow bundle-level and prompt-level ACL rules so teams can share, restrict, or expose prompts with fine granularity.
- Add signing support so that curated bundles can be cryptographically attested (key registry + signer identity).
- Provide migration and compatibility plan for existing golden datasets and promptsets to avoid eval regressions during rollout.

Out of scope:
- Full migration automation for thousands of community promptsets (will be a follow-up incremental project).
- UI polish beyond MVP access controls and version view.

Why this matters: Eval gating and regression detection require that the exact artifact executed during a baseline run is reproducible and auditable. Current practice mixes ephemeral titles/notes with content, causing noisy diffs and accidental regressions. Separating ACLs and signing from content hash reduces accidental drift and enables automated gating based on immutable fingerprints.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Each new or edited prompt bundle stored in golden registry gets assigned a SHA256 content fingerprint computed only over prompts and structured test harness input; 2) UI shows fingerprint and history; 3) Bundle-level ACLs support allow/deny lists and team roles; 4) Signing can be attached to a bundle with signer id and signature blob; 5) Eval pipeline can reference a bundle by fingerprint and produce deterministic results; 6) Migration guide exists and we've migrated 3 pilot bundles with no eval deltas observed in staging dashboard.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Malik: Created ticket after cross-functional kickoff with Eng, Security, and Design. Initial ask came from SRE and Eval teams who saw two production regressions traced to implicit prompt edits. See meeting notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EVAL/2026-02-19+-+Prompt+Bundle+Kickoff

2026-02-25 - Luis Ortega: Design review notes: prefer content-addressed fingerprint (SHA256) over timestamp-based IDs; signature model should allow multiple signers (author + approver); ACL should be enforced at API layer and surfaced in Console. Action: ENG to prototype hashing util and ACL schema. (Assigned ENG-15802 for feasibility).

2026-03-03 - Priya Nair (Eng): ENG feasibility: minimal runtime change for eval runner to accept fingerprint; backend needs a fingerprint index for quick resolution; estimate 8 dev points for MVP (index + CRUD + API). We'll need a short DB migration to store fingerprint column.

2026-03-08 - Maya Chen (Security): Security review requested. Recommendation: signer keys should be managed with KMS/HSM; adopt a signing policy that prevents developer-only self-signing for production-locked bundles. Follow-up: produce threat model by 2026-03-18.

2026-03-10 - Aisha Malik: Moved to In Progress. Created prototype PR for hashing and storage schema. Coordinating pilot migration for two golden bundles owned by Search and Rerank teams. Added UX mockups to Drive.
decision_log: 2026-02-25: Use content-addressed SHA256 fingerprint computed over canonicalized prompt JSON (ordering and whitespace normalized) — accepted.
2026-02-25: Signing model will support multiple signatures; each signature stores signer id, key version, and signature blob. Verification uses KMS-managed public keys — accepted.
2026-03-03: ACL rules will be enforced at registry API level and mirrored in Console; policy engine deferred to later iteration — accepted for MVP.
2026-03-08: Require HSM/KMS-backed signing for bundles promoted to 'locked' production status; dev-signed bundles allowed in sandbox — security approved pending threat model.
2026-03-09: Rollout strategy: pilot -> gated migration with canary evals -> full migration. Canary must show 0 blocking regressions for 48 hours before broad switch.
